The use of noise abatement barriers would have significant adverse economic effect on highway oriented commercial and industrial buildings along the proposed route to be improved.
3. The Village of Park Forest has a twenty (20) foot right-of-way along the south side of Lincoln Highway. Particular attention was devoted to the buildings located between Indiana Street and Rockwell Street. Within these limits the residential structures do not have access to Lincoln Highway.
In order to provide protection to residents contiguous to the highway the Village of Park Forest Planted a double row of honeysuckles some fifteen (15) years ago. The proposed cross section for Lincoln Highway would adjust the south curb line to within three and one-half (3½) feet of the outer row of shrubs. Therefore, the Illinois Department of Transportation requested the Village of Park Forest to pass a resolution utilizing their Motor Fuel Tax Funds to pay for the replacement screen plantings.
The amount of money spent by the Village of Park Forest for the planting replacement will be credited against the amount of money due the State of Illinois for modernization of existing traffic signals.
Property lines platted with the county recorders office for future development have been shown. It is to be noted that the property has not been developed or may not be developed at the time of location approval. If we were to consider noise barriers the damage to the proposed sub-division could be such as to cause the developer not to be able to improve the property in question.
The proposed use of the land would have to be re-engineered causing an economic hardship on the developer. Streets, lot layouts, public utilities, building and zoning information would have to be re-submitted for local approval. This could also affect the mortgage on this development.
